Turbo Chook is a small, transparent LLM coding agent written in R. This
vignette walks through: the loop, then `handfish()` (the teaching version, where you approve every step), then
the full agent and the Ralph Loop.

## The loop

Every agent here runs the same three steps:

1. **THINK**: send a message to the LLM. It replies with text and, optionally,
   one or more tool calls.
2. **ACT**: run the tool(s) in R.
3. **OBSERVE**: send the tools' results back to the LLM.

... and repeat until the LLM calls `task_complete`.

API calls go through the `ellmer` package, so any provider and model ellmer
supports will work.

## Before you start

```{r}
devtools::install_github("cbrown5/turbochook")
```

You need an API key for your provider, e.g. `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` in
`~/.Renviron`. The easiest way to add it is `usethis::edit_r_environ()`.

## Start with handfish

`handfish()` is the same loop with four tools. It is for learning

```{r}
turbochook::handfish("Make a file called hello.R that prints 'hi', then run it.")
```

**It asks before it does anything.** Every tool call is printed, then waits:

```
→ run_r_code
source("hello.R")
  Run this run_r_code call? [y/N]
```

Only `y` (or `yes`) runs it. Anything else, including a stray keypress or
Enter, is a no. When you decline, the agent is told it was refused and asks you
what to do instead. `task_complete` is the one tool that isn't gated; it only ends the session.

Its loop has an extra step in front of `turbochook()`'s:

1. **THINK**: the LLM replies with text and, optionally, tool calls.
2. **ASK**: show you the call and wait.
3. **ACT**: run it, if you said yes.
4. **OBSERVE**: send the result back.

### Try it on the example data

The package has a real analysis to try an agent on.
`fish_coral_cover_sites` is reef survey data from 49 sites in the Solomon
Islands: counts of juvenile bumphead parrotfish ('topa') and benthic cover
measured at the same places. Cover is a count of survey points, so divide by
`n_pts` for per cent cover.

```{r}
head(turbochook::fish_coral_cover_sites)
?turbochook::fish_coral_cover_sites        # the variables, and where they came from
```

`glm-readme.md` is the brief that goes with it: the aims, the modelling
approach (negative binomial GLM, model selection by likelihood ratio test), the
workflow, and the shape of the report to write. `glm_example_setup()` copies
the brief and the data into a folder, laid out the way the brief expects.

```{r}
wd <- turbochook::glm_example_setup()
list.files(wd, recursive = TRUE)
#> "data/fish-coral-cover-sites.csv" "glm-readme.md"
```

Pointing `handfish()` at a piece of it is a good way to watch the loop work,
one approved call at a time:

```{r}
turbochook::handfish(
  "Read glm-readme.md, then read the data and describe what is in it.",
  wd = wd
)
```

### Running it unattended

!! Be careful, can cause damage to your computer, such as delete files !! 

The console prompt needs an interactive session. Pass your own `approve`
function to decide in code:

```{r}
# approve everything
handfish("...", approve = function(name, args) TRUE)

# approve reads, refuse everything else
handfish("...", approve = function(name, args) name == "read_file")
```

It takes the tool's name and a list of its arguments, and returns `TRUE` to let
the call run.

### How handfish and turbochook functions compare

| | `turbochook()` | `handfish()` |
|---|---|---|
| Tools | 6 | 4: `read_file`, `write_file`, `run_r_code`, `task_complete` |
| Where code runs | a separate `callr` session | **your R session** |
| Safety | sandbox, no approval | **approval, no sandbox** |
| Vision, skills, retries, `run_r_script` | yes | no |

`turbochook()` keeps the agent at arm's length so it can work unattended;
`handfish()` lets it into your session but makes you sign off on every step.
Read each call before you accept it: `run_r_code` runs in your own session, so
it can do anything you can.

## The full agent

```{r}
turbochook::turbochook("Load data.csv, plot cover against distance and save it as plot.png")
```

The agent works in the current folder (or `wd = "some/folder"`). It returns
(invisibly) a list with the `summary`, `status`, `steps`, `tool_calls`,
`tokens`, `cost` and the `chat`, so you can keep talking to it.

It has six tools: `read_file`, `write_file`, `edit_file`, `run_r_code`,
`run_r_script` (runs a project script in a fresh R process, like `Rscript`) and
`task_complete`.

### Pick your provider and model

Pass any ellmer chat object. A copy is used, so your object isn't changed.

```{r}
turbochook("...", chat = ellmer::chat_anthropic(model = "claude-haiku-5-5"))
turbochook("...", chat = ellmer::chat_openrouter(model = "qwen/qwen3.8-27b"))
turbochook("...", chat = ellmer::chat_ollama(model = "llama3.3"))
```

### Limits, to manage costs

```{r}
turbochook("...", max_steps = 30, max_tool_calls = 60, timeout = 60, max_result_chars = 5000)
```

- `max_steps`: most LLM replies.
- `max_tool_calls`: most tool calls (`task_complete` is always allowed, so the
  agent can sum up).
- `timeout`: seconds before a `run_r_code` or `run_r_script` call is stopped.
- `max_result_chars`: long tool results are cut short before going to the LLM.

### Add your own tools

Make them with `ellmer::tool()` and pass them in a list. They run in your R
session, not the sandbox.

```{r}
count_rows <- ellmer::tool(
  function(path) nrow(read.csv(path)),
  name = "count_rows",
  description = "Count the rows in a csv file.",
  arguments = list(path = ellmer::type_string("Path to the csv file."))
)
turbochook("How many rows are in data.csv?", tools = list(count_rows))
```

### Vision

```{r}
turbochook("Make a plot of the data, then check it looks right", vision = TRUE)
turbochook("...", vision = ellmer::chat_openai(model = "gpt-5"))  # any vision model
```

This adds a `look_at_image(path, question)` tool. It sends the image to a
separate vision chat (Claude Sonnet 5.5 by default). Its tokens and cost are
added to the totals.

### AGENTS.md and skills

- If the folder has an `AGENTS.md`, it is added to the system prompt.
- Skills go in `skills/<name>/SKILL.md` or `skills/<name>.md`. Only each
  skill's name, description (from a `description:` line in the YAML header, or
  the first line) and path go in the system prompt. The agent reads the full
  file with `read_file` when it needs it.

### The sandbox

The agent's `run_r_code` calls run in a separate `callr::r_session()`, with a
timeout and a soft internet block (proxies pointed at a dead address), and the
file tools are held to the project folder. **callr gives isolation, not
security** — the child process runs as you, with all your permissions, so it
can still delete files or shell out. For real isolation run the agent in
Docker, a separate user account or VM, or under `sandbox-exec` / `bubblewrap`,
and keep the project under git.

### Rate limits

Every API call is retried when the error looks like a rate limit (`429`,
`Too Many Requests`, `rate limit`, `throttle`, plus Anthropic's
`overloaded`/`529`). The waits are 2s, 4s, 8s, 16s, ... plus some jitter, for
up to `max_retries` (default 5) tries. You can use `with_retry()` in your own
code too.

## The Ralph Loop

The example analysis is a long job for one context, so it suits the Ralph Loop:
fresh agents on the same prompt, again and again, until the job is done.

```{r}
turbochook::ralph("Read glm-readme.md and do the analysis it asks for.",
                  wd = wd, max_loops = 10, max_cost = 5)
```

Each loop is a fresh `turbochook()` run (a clean context) with the same prompt.
The agents pass notes to each other in `PROGRESS.md`. The loop stops when an
agent writes a `RALPH_DONE` file (only allowed once the whole task is checked),
or at `max_loops` / `max_cost`. The done signal is a file, not a word in the
summary, because models write things like "not RALPH_DONE yet".

Other arguments are passed on to `turbochook()`:

```{r}
turbochook::ralph(
  "Write R functions for each analysis in plan.md, with tests.",
  max_loops = 10,
  max_cost = 2,                       # dollars, if ellmer knows the price
  chat = ellmer::chat_anthropic(model = "claude-haiku-5-5"),
  max_steps = 20                      # passed on to turbochook()
)
```

## Where to look next

| File | What it does |
|---|---|
| `R/agent.R` | `turbochook()`: setup, the hooks and the loop |
| `R/handfish.R` | `handfish()`: the smaller teaching agent, and its tools |
| `R/tools.R` | the six default tools, the vision tool, path checks |
| `R/sandbox.R` | starts the callr session and runs code in it |
| `R/prompt.R` | system prompt, AGENTS.md, skills directory |
| `R/display.R` | everything printed to the screen |
| `R/retry.R` | rate limit retries with backoff |
| `R/ralph.R` | the Ralph Loop |
